claims.text: The Hallucination Ontology (HALO) is a formal, extensible ontology written in OWL for representing hallucinations in large language models.
HALO supports six different types of hallucinations known to arise in LLMs.
HALO supports provenance and experimental metadata for LLM hallucinations.
A dataset of hallucinations was inductively gathered across multiple independent Web sources.
HALO can model the inductively gathered hallucination dataset and answer competency questions.

evidence.description: The authors present 'the Hallucination Ontology or HALO, a formal, extensible ontology written in OWL'.
HALO 'currently offers support for six different types of hallucinations known to arise in LLMs'.
HALO includes 'support for provenance and experimental metadata'.
The paper reports collecting 'a dataset containing hallucinations that we inductively gathered across multiple independent Web sources'.
The authors show 'that HALO can be successfully used to model this dataset and answer competency questions'.

methodologies.name: Hallucination Ontology (HALO)
methodologies.description: A formal, extensible ontology written in OWL to describe, represent, and categorize LLM hallucinations with relevant metadata.

limitations.text: A formal model for describing and representing LLM hallucinations with relevant metadata at a fine-grained level is lacking in existing work.
